content: Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control, Orlando, Florida, has been awarded an $825,975,480 modification (P00020) to previously awarded (FA8682-24-C-B001) for the Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile and Long Range Anti-Ship Missile Large Lot procurement. This modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $10,480,052,550 from $9,654,077,070. Work will be performed in Orlando, Florida, and is expected to be completed July 31, 2030. Fiscal 2024 missile procurement funds in the amount of $2,150,000; fiscal 2024 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,453,033; fiscal 2025 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $219,510,682; fiscal 2025 missile procurement funds in the amount of $378,735; fiscal 2026 missile procurement funds in the amount of $72,767,776; fiscal 2026 weapons procurement funds (Navy) in the amount of $49,219,714; fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $4,159,804; fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $686,013; and Foreign Military Sales funds in the amount of $11,070,988, are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Eglin Air Force Base, Florida, is the contracting activity.

CAE USA Inc., Tampa, Florida, has been awarded a $45,319,364 firm-fixed-price contract for a full flight simulator and logistics support package. This contract provides for the acquisition and installation of one Federal Aviation Administration, Level D qualified 747-8i full flight simulator at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, and the acquisition of an initial logistics support package. Work will be performed in Tampa, Florida; Saint-Laurent, Quebec, Canada; and Joint Base Andrews, Maryland; and is expected to be completed by March 30, 2029. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2025 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $43,628,111 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Lifecycle Management Center, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity (FA8641-26-C-B002).

Lockheed Martin Corp., Liverpool, New York, was awarded a $257,278,109 firm-fixed-price, cost-plus-fixed-fee, and cost-only modification to a previously awarded contract (N00024-23-C-6411) to exercise options for production, spares, production support material, engineering support, and hardware repair of components for MK 48 Heavyweight Torpedo All Up Round in support of the MK 48 MOD 7 Heavyweight Torpedo program. This contract combines purchases for the Navy, the Royal Australian Navy, and the Foreign Military Sales program. Work will be performed in Liverpool, New York (57%); Clearwater, Florida (37%); and Braintree, Massachusetts (6%), and is expected to be completed by September 2029. Fiscal 2025 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $150,647,159 (62%); fiscal 2026 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of (7%); fiscal 2024 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,216,670 (1%); and funding from foreign partners in the amount of $74,799,495 (30%), will be obligated at the time of award. Funding in the amount of $1,216,670 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity. (Awarded Sept. 3, 2026).

BAE Systems Land & Armaments L.P., Maple Grove, Minnesota, is awarded a $38,199,786 cost-plus-incentive-fee modification to previously awarded contract (N00024-24-F-5322) for the procurement of two MK 45 Mod 4 overhauls. Work will be performed in Louisville, Kentucky, and is expected to be completed by March 2030. Fiscal 2024 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $38,199,786 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

Moog Military Aircraft LLC, Elma, New York, is being awarded $16,547,505 firm-fixed-price contract for the overhaul of the swashplate actuator (7RH 1680-014749949) supporting V-22 sustainment. Work will be performed in East Aurora, New York; and Fleet Readiness Center East (FRC-E), Havelock, North Carolina, as part of a public-private partnership between Moog and FRC-E. Work is expected to be completed by March 2029. Fiscal 2026 working capital funds in the amount of $16,547,505 will be committed at the time of award and those funds will not expire. One source was solicited for this sole-source requirement pursuant to the authority set forth in 10 U.S. Code 3204 (c)(1) and one offer was received. Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon System Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania is the contracting activity (N00383-26-C-BA21).

Huntington Ingalls Inc., Pascagoula, Mississippi, is awarded a $13,217,537 cost-plus-award-fee contract for Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) Planning Yard support for advanced planning, class engineering, and primary support of the modernization of the LCS Class. This contract includes options which, if exercised, would bring the cumulative value of this contract to $742,848,205. Work will be performed in Pascagoula, Mississippi, and is expected to be completed by September 2027. If all options are exercised, work will continue through September 2033. Fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funding in the amount of $13,217,537 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the System for Award Management website, with two offers received. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N00024-26-C-4313).

National Steel and Shipbuilding Co., was awarded an $11,423,786 fixed-price incentive modification (N0002424C2301A00023) to a previously awarded contract (N00024-24-C-2301) to provide production, engineering, and material support to incorporate the requirements of T-AO engineering change proposals. Work will be performed in San Diego, California, and is expected to be completed by January 2035. Fiscal 2025 shipbuilding and conversion, Navy funds in the amount of $3,185,697 (98%); and fiscal 2024 shipbuilding and conversion, Navy funds in the amount of $79,448 (2%), will be obligated at the time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Supervisor of Shipbuilding, Conversion, and Repair, Bath, Maine, is the contracting activity. (Awarded Sept. 4, 2026).

Amentum Services Inc., Germantown, Maryland, is awarded a $10,192,466 modification (P00016) to a previously awarded indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract (N0042123D0012). This modification increases the contract ceiling as a result of an updated collective bargaining agreement for contractor logistics support, maintenance, and logistical support services for the Navy’s F-16A/B/C/D aircraft fleet. Work will be performed in Fallon, Nevada, and is expected to be completed in August 2027. No funds will be obligated at the time of award; funds will be obligated on individual orders as they are issued. The base contract was competitively procured. Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

Fairbanks Morse, Beloit, Wisconsin, is awarded a $9,947,506 firm-fixed-price task order for the acquisition and delivery of critical Emergency Diesel Generator renewal materials to support complete engine overhauls for active Navy submarines. Work under this order will be performed at the contractor's facilities in Beloit, Wisconsin, and is expected to be completed by May 30, 2027. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance, Navy funds in the amount of $9,947,506 will be obligated at the time of award and will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This task order contains options which, if exercised, will bring the cumulative value of the order to $11,572,255. This order was procured on a sole source basis under Basic Ordering Agreement (N6449826G1004). Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity (N6449826FX244).

Nitradyn LLC, Tampa, Florida, was awarded a $581,160,062 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract to design, construct and commission a facility to manufacture Insensitive Munition eXplosive - 104. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Aug. 9, 2030. Army Contracting Command, Rock Island Arsenal Illinois, is the contracting activity (W519TC-26-F-A454).

BCG Federal Corp., Bethesda, Maryland, was awarded a $100,000,000 firm-fixed-price contract (HT003826FE012), in support of the logical follow-on to the successful completion of the Design-to-Outcome Task Order Year 4 and Core Task Order Year Four. The contract provides Workforce 3.0, a fully managed end-to-end solution supporting the Program Executive Office, Defense Healthcare Management Systems (PEO DHMS) mid-office and back-office functions across the full PEO DHMS product portfolio. The Year Five Core Task Order continues execution of the Workforce 3.0 solution and implements the agreed upon Year Five Design-to-Outcome task order. The period of performance is Aug. 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds were obligated at the time of award. The place of performance is Arlington, Virginia. The Defense Health Agency, Defense Healthcare Management Systems Contracting Division, Arlington, Virginia, is the contracting activity. (Awarded July 30, 2026).

Heartland Manufacturing Inc.,* Edgewood, New York, has been awarded a maximum $27,175,061 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for dress shirts. This was a competitive acquisition with three responses received. This is a five-year contract with no option periods. The ordering period end date is Sept. 8, 2031. Using military service is Army. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2031 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPE1C1-26-D-0087).

The Boeing Co., Layton, Utah, has been awarded a maximum $23,175,320 firm-fixed-price contract for intercontinental ballistic missile cable assemblies. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a four-year two-month contract with no option periods. The performance completion date is Oct. 31, 2030. Using military service is Air Force. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support, Hill Air Force Base, Utah (SPRHA2‐26-C-0001).

Exelan Pharmaceuticals Inc., Boca Raton, Florida, has been awarded a maximum $15,891,410 fixed-price with economic-price-adjustment, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for various pharmaceuticals. This was a competitive acquisition with 30 responses received. This is a one-year base contract with nine one-year option periods. The performance completion date is Sept. 8, 2027. Using customers are Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps and federal civilian agencies. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2027 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPE2D0-26-D-0002).

UPDATE: Hill-Rom Inc., Batesville, Indiana (SPE2DH-26-D-0014, $42,500,000), has been added as an awardee to the multiple award contract for medical equipment and accessories for the Defense Logistics Agency Electronic Catalog, issued against solicitation SPE2DH-21-R-0002 and awarded Feb. 10, 2022. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

UPDATE: Peter Brasseler Holdings LLC, Savannah, Georgia (SPE2DF-26-D-0021, $42,000,000), has been added as an awardee to the multiple award contract for dental supplies and equipment for the Defense Logistics Agency Electronic Catalog, issued against solicitation SPE2DE-25-R-0002 and awarded Feb. 12, 2026. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

Northrop Grumman Systems Corp., Rolling Meadows, Illinois, was awarded a $4,838,487,318 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for full rate production of the Common Infrared Countermeasure. One bid was solicited with one received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 30, 2035. Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is the contracting activity (W58RGZ-26-D-0056).

Conti Federal Services LLC, Orlando, Florida, was awarded a $74,787,155 firm-fixed-price contract, with a total cumulative face value of $74,978,377. The contract provides for construction of a B-21 program radio frequency and measurements hangar facility with one B-21 aircraft position, associated back shops, material storage, and administrative and facility support spaces. Bids were solicited via the internet with three received. Work will be performed in Whiteman Air Force Base, Missouri, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 25, 2029. Fiscal 2026 military construction, defense-wide funds in the amount of $74,787,155 were obligated at the time of award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City, Missouri, is the contracting activity (W912DQ-26-C-A048).

Stantec Consulting Services Inc., Denver, Colorado, was awarded a $12,580,830 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for engineering design support services for the Albeni Falls Fish Passage Facility Project. Bids were solicited via the internet with seven received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Aug. 31, 2028. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Seattle, Washington, is the contracting activity (W912DW-26-F-A094). (Awarded Sept. 5, 2026).

Creation Gardens Inc., doing business as What Chefs Want, Louisville, Kentucky, has been awarded a maximum $496,849,673 firm-fixed-price with economic-price-adjustment, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for fresh fruits and vegetables. This was a competitive acquisition with three responses received. This is a five-year contract with no option periods. Location of performance is Illinois, with a Sept. 7, 2031, ordering period end date. Using customers are Army, Air Force, and the Department of Agriculture. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2031 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPE300-26-D-P450).

Dominion Privatization Virginia, Richmond, Virginia, has been awarded an estimated $26,978,430 modification (P00350) to a 50‐year contract (SP0600-06-C-8252) with no option periods for privatizing additional electrical infrastructure located at Humphreys Engineering Center. This is a fixed-price with prospective-price-redetermination contract. The performance completion date is Aug. 1, 2057. Using military service is Army. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2078 Army operations and maintenance funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Energy, Fort Belvoir, Virginia.

Peckham Vocational Industries Inc.,* Lansing, Michigan, has been awarded a maximum $11,582,550 fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for cold weather caps. This is a five-year contract with no option periods. The ordering period end date is Sept. 7, 2031. Using military services are Air Force, Navy, and Marine Corps. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2031 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPE1C1-26-D-N022).

Raytheon Co., McKinney, Texas, has been awarded a maximum $10,057,499 firm-fixed-price delivery order (SPRPA1-26-F-SV0F) against a five-year basic ordering agreement (N00383-23-G-SV01) for F/A-18 spare parts. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated by Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a two-year contract with no option periods. The performance completion date is June 30, 2028. Using military service is Navy. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2028 Navy defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

Aerospace & Commercial Technologies LLC, Fort Worth, Texas, has been awarded a maximum $9,274,300 firm-fixed-price contract for F-16 horizontal stabilizers. This was a competitive acquisition with one response received. This is a two-year ten-month contract with no option periods. The performance completion date is July 3, 2029. Using military service is Air Force. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support Hill, Air Force Base, Utah (SPRHA4‐26-C-0045).

Aviation Systems Engineering Co., Lexington Park, Maryland, is awarded a $288,823,141 cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price and cost reimbursable, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract to procure administrative, business, engineering, information technology, sustainment, operations, and program management across all life cycle phases necessary to ensure continuity of services in support of legacy and new components, subsystems, systems, sensors, and mission avionics for naval air platforms to include engineering, management, technical labor, materials and equipment needed for technology assessment and development, fabrication, prototyping, laboratory and field experiments, ship and air exercises, test, installation, system integration, sustainment, aircrew training, fleet assistance and training, procurement activities, and environmental compliance documentation in support of Navy, Marine Corps, other government agencies, allies, and Foreign Military Sales customers. Work locations will be identified at the individual task order level and is expected to be completed in March 2032. No funds will be obligated at the time of award; funds will be obligated on individual task orders as they are issued. This contract was not competitively procured. Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity (N0042126D1004).

Marine Ventures International Inc.,* Stuart, Florida, is awarded a $64,991,667 hybrid, cost-plus-fixed-fee and firm-fixed price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for the operation, maintenance and repair of the MV Independence. Work will be performed at Port Hueneme, California, and primarily in the coastal waters of California, Oregon, and Washington, and is expected to be completed by March 2032. The maximum dollar value, including the base period and one option, is $64,991,667. A minimum guarantee of $10,000 will be funded with Fiscal 2026 Navy working capital funds to satisfy the minimum guarantee. Future task orders will be primarily funded by research, development, test and evaluation funds. This contract was competitively procured via SAM.gov website, with three offers received. Naval Facilities Engineering and Expeditionary Warfare Center, Port Hueneme, California, is the contracting activity (N39430-26-D-4007).

IrvinGQ Ltd., Llangeinor, Bridgend, United Kingdom, is awarded a $14,743,469 firm-fixed-price contract modification for Option Year One production of the MK-59 Floating Decoy System. Work will be performed in Bridgend, United Kingdom (64%); West Fargo, North Dakota (16%); York, United Kingdom (11%); Bloomfield, Connecticut (2%); and various other locations each less than 2% (7%), and is expected to be completed by March 2028. Fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $14,743,469 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was not competitively procured in accordance with 10 U.S. Code 2304(c)(1) (only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements). The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N00024-26-C-5524).

Huntington Ingalls Inc., Ingalls Shipbuilding Division, Pascagoula, Mississippi, was awarded a $12,983,399 cost-plus-fixed-fee, with a special performance incentive, modification (A00405) to a previously awarded contract (N00024-21-C-4205) to purchase commercial material for planning yard support for procurement of common rail upgrade for LPD17 Class USS New Orleans (LPD 18). Fiscal 2026 other procurements (Navy) funds in the amount of $12,983,399 was obligated at time of award, which will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity. (Awarded Sept. 2, 2026).

Aerospace Training Systems Partners JV LLP,* Norman, Oklahoma, is awarded a $10,096,092 firm-fixed-price contract (N6134026C1017) for the design, fabrication, installation, integration, testing, and delivery of P-8A Operational Flight Trainer projection system upgrades for the Navy and Royal Australian Air Force. Work will be performed in Jacksonville, Florida (50%); Oak Harbor, Washington (40%); and Edinburgh, Australia (10%), and is expected to be completed in November 2028. Fiscal 2026 aircraft procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $8,202,118 and Royal Australian Air Force cooperative funds in the amount of $1,893,974 will be obligated at the time of award. This contract was competitively procured as a small-business set-aside, with four offers received. Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division, Orlando, Florida, is the contracting activity.

Superior Forge and Steel, Lima, Ohio (FA8681-26-D-B003, FA8681-26-F-B045); Ellwood National Forge, Irvine, Pennsylvania (FA8681-26-D-B004, FA8681-26-F-B046); Faxon Machining LLC, Cincinnati, Ohio (FA8681-26-D-B005, FA8681-26-F-B047); and Grand Valley Manufacturing, Titusville, Pennsylvania (FA8681-26-D-B006, FA8681-26-F-B048), were awarded a cumulative maximum ceiling of $149,000,000 firm-fixed-price, cost-type indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contracts for large penetrator warhead case assembly production. This contract provides for the manufacturing of the assemblies, including the production of associated full and subscale variants. Work will be performed at Superior Forge and Steel, Lima, Ohio; Ellwood National Forge, Irvine, Pennsylvania; Faxon Machining LLC, Cincinnati, Ohio; and Grand Valley Manufacturing, Titusville, Pennsylvania; and is expected to be completed by Sept. 7, 2033, if the option to extend is executed. These contracts were competitive acquisitions, and four offers were received. Fiscal 2026, research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $10,000 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Eglin Air Force Base, Florida, is the contracting activity.

PKL Services Inc., Poway, California, has been awarded a $25,240,523 modification (P00017) to previously awarded (FA4897-22-C-0015) for Republic of Singapore Air Force flight operations and maintenance support training. This modification provides for an additional 12 months of performance. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $114,413,846 from $89,173,323. Work will be performed at Mountain Home Air Force Base, Idaho, and is expected to be completed by Sept. 30, 2027. This contract involves foreign military sales to the Republic of Singapore. Foreign Military Sales funds in the amount of $25,240,523 are being obligated at time of award. The 366th Contracting Squadron, Mountain Home AFB, Idaho, is the contracting activity.

Singularity Security Group, Mclean, Virginia, has been awarded a $24,999,999 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for site security management and construction surveillance technician services. This contract provides construction security surveillance for secure construction projects. Work will be performed at Beale Air Force Base, California, and is expected to be completed by Sept. 30, 2031. This contract was a competitive acquisition, and two offers were received. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $5,000 are being obligated at the time of award. The 9th Contracting Squadron, Beale AFB, California, is the contracting activity (FA4686-26-A-P001).

Pratt and Whitney, RTX Corp., East Hartford, Connecticut, has been awarded a $19,314,136 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for contractor engineering and technical services. This contract provides for advisory engineering and technical services until organic engineering capability is developed. Work will be performed at Air National Guard installations; Argentina; Greece; Korea; Egypt; Indonesia; Jordan; Morocco; Iraq; Taiwan; Thailand; and Saudi Arabia and is expected to be complete by March 15, 2029. This contract involves Foreign Military Sales to Argentina; Greece; Korea; Egypt; Indonesia; Jordan; Morocco; Iraq; Taiwan; Thailand; Saudi Arabia. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $1,233,469 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity (FA8604-26-D-B007).

Clark Construction Group LLC, Bethesda, Maryland, was awarded a $121,787,000 firm-fixed-price contract for construction of a cybersecurity operations facility. Bids were solicited via the internet with three received. Work will be performed in Fort Meade, Maryland, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 2, 2029. Fiscal 2024 military construction, defense-wide funds in the amount of $121,787,000 are being obligated at the time of award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Baltimore, Maryland, is the contracting activity (W912DR-26-C-A019).

SupplyCore Inc.,* Rockford, Illinois, has been awarded a maximum $90,000,000 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for facilities maintenance, repair and operations supplies. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a 396-day bridge contract with no option periods. Locations of performance are Louisiana and Texas. with an Oct. 2, 2027, ordering period end date. Using customers are Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps and Coast Guard. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2027 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPE8E3-26-D-0013).

Update: Revision Military Ltd., Essex Junction, Vermont (SPE2DF-26-D-0014, $37,500,000), has been added as an awardee to the multiple award contract for optical frames for the Defense Logistics Agency Electronic Catalog, issued against solicitation SPE2DE-24-R-0001 and awarded Sept. 11, 2024. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

The Boeing Co., Ridley Park, Pennsylvania, is being awarded a $55,387,192 firm-fixed-price order (W91215-16-G-0001) for basic ordering agreement H9224126FE046 for the procurement of the Active Parallel Actuator System, and associated parts, in support of the MH-47G Program. The majority of the work will be performed in Ridley Park, Pennsylvania, and is expected to be completed by August 2033. U.S. Special Operations Command, MacDill Air Force Base, Florida, is the contracting activity.

NAG LLC, Virginia Beach, Virginia, is awarded a $39,441,631 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for the procurement of shipboard Radar Tank Level Indicator computer hardware. Under this contract, NAG LLC will provide materials required for the design, development, fabrication, testing, repair, and fleet implementation of TLI systems. Work will be performed in Virginia Beach, Virginia, and is expected to be completed by Sept. 1, 2031. Fiscal 2024 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $2,152,562 will be obligated at the time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the System for Award Management website, with one responsible offer received. The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity (N64498-26-D-1001).

General Dynamics Mission Systems, Quincy, Massachusetts, is awarded a $15,147,625 cost-plus-incentive-fee and firm-fixed-price modification to previously awarded contract (N00024-24-C-6315) to exercise options for the Mining Expendable Delivery Unmanned Submarine Asset. Work will be performed in Quincy, Massachusetts, and is expected to be completed by February 2028. Fiscal year 2025 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $15,147,625 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington Navy Yard, D.C., is the contracting activity.

Integer Technologies LLC,* Columbia, South Carolina, is awarded a $10,220,910 modification (CLIN 0002) to contract (N0001426C1129) for research and development for cyber-physical systems in Navy infrastructure. This contract provides for the exercise of Option One. The Louisiana State University and Integer Technologies partnership is advancing a cyber-physical resilience framework designed to safeguard the Navy’s maritime platforms. This proposal for Navy Embedded Systems outlines a structured, phased approach that begins with a comprehensive assessment of emerging cyber-physical vulnerabilities and culminates in the operational deployment of defense solutions across naval vessels and shore facilities. By integrating advanced simulation models, real-time dashboards and edge-hardening techniques, the program aims to deliver actionable insights that enhance mission effectiveness and protect critical systems from sophisticated adversaries. Work will be performed in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and is expected to be completed in March 2030. The amount of this action is $10,220,910, increasing the total cumulative contract value to $10,468,515. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $10,220,910 are obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Office of Naval Research, Arlington, Virginia, is the contracting activity.

Sierra Nevada Corp., Englewood, Colorado, has been awarded a $31,789,335 cost-reimbursement-fixed-fee, cost-reimbursement-no-fee, and firm-fixed-price contract for non-recurring engineering. This contract provides for design, development, and analysis of a post-production modification kit to convert a standard production XC-130J aircraft into a ski-equipped LC-130J.  Work will be performed at Colorado Springs, Colorado, and is expected to be completed March 27, 2028. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2025 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $31,789,335 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Lifecycle Management Center, Warner Robins, Georgia, is the contracting activity (FA8509-26-C-B001). (Awarded Sept. 1, 2026).

Aptima Inc., Woburn, Massachusetts, (FA2384-26-D-B004); and BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems Inc., Broomfield, Colorado (FA2384-26-D-B009), were awarded a ceiling $26,200,000 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for holistic models for decision-making. This contract provides for research to develop computational and mathematical models that simulate the effects of operational environment on warfighter performance. Work will be performed in Woburn, Massachusetts; Broomfield, Colorado; and Dayton, Ohio; and is expected to be completed by Aug. 24, 2034. These contracts were competitive acquisitions, and nine offers were received. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $9,836 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Research Laboratory, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity. (Awarded Sept. 1, 2026).

BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems Inc., Boulder, Colorado, was awarded a $18,890,685 cost-plus-fixed-fee contract for Infrared Radiation Effects Laboratory operation and improvements. This contract provides for radiometric and radiation characterizations of focal plane arrays (FPA) and associated devices. Work will be performed in Boulder, Colorado, and is expected to be completed by Dec. 2, 2031. This contract was a competitive acquisition, and one offer was received. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $420,737 are being obligated at time of award. Integer Technologies LLC,* Columbia, South Carolina, is awarded a $9,769,318 option exercise contract modification (P00002) to a contract (N0001425C2204) for the "Intelligent Autonomous Systems for Seabed Warfare" effort. The modification provides continuing science and technology research into an operational decision-support tool for intelligent autonomous systems conducting seabed warfare and undersea missions. The tool consists of physics and data-based models, deployed at the edge, that allow for real-time processing of seabed warfare sensor datasets, monitoring of the evolving environmental conditions in an area of operation, and real-time adaptation of onboard data collection, data processing, and vehicle command parameters to maximize the likelihood of mission success. The tool has the potential to improve the intelligence and independence of autonomous systems employed on seabed warfare missions, to enable multi-domain seabed warfare missions, and allow for autonomous systems to operate for significantly longer with minimal human intervention. The project will develop and demonstrate the application of edge deployed modeling and simulation tools, combined with artificial intelligence and machine learning to real-time decision making for intelligent autonomous systems. This capability is foundational to the Navy's envisioned long-duration, forward deployments of autonomous systems, particularly underwater autonomous systems, for seabed warfare missions in contested maritime regions. Work will be performed in Columbia, South Carolina, and is expected to be completed in July 2029. The total cumulative value of this contract is $24,803,999, inclusive of base period ($4,377,498), Option One ($10,657,183), and Option Two ($9,769,318). The base is fully funded and Option One exercised. Option Two will be incrementally funded with an initial obligation of $6,389,978. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $6,389,978 are obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Office of Naval Research, Arlington, Virginia, is the contracting activity.

Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $2,271,075 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Research Laboratory, Kirtland AFB, New Mexico, is the contracting activity (FA9453-26-D-X007).

JE DUNN Construction Co., Kansas City, Missouri, has been awarded a $45,770,554 unpriced change order definitization modification (PZ0021) to a previously awarded contract (FA8903-19-C-0021) for repair of the cadet chapel at the U.S. Air Force Academy. These contracts provide for launch services delivering NSS payloads into their intended orbits. The location and period of performance will be determined at the task order level. These contracts were competitive acquisitions, and three offers were received. Fiscal 2026 space procurement funds in the amount of $10,000,000 are being obligated at time of award. Space Systems Command, Space Access, Los Angeles Air Force Base, California, is the contracting activity.

General Dynamics Mission Systems, Quincy, Massachusetts, was awarded a $13,811,780 cost-plus-incentive-fee; $31,173 cost-plus-fixed-fee; and $127,261 cost reimbursable, modification to a previously awarded contract (N00024-24-C-6315) to exercise options for Mining Expendable Delivery Unmanned Submarine Asset prototype systems, software development, Ashore Support Equipment, and Engineering Services. Corvid Technologies LLC,* Mooresville, North Carolina, is awarded a $9,250,500 modification to a previously awarded contract (N6339425C0003) for the design, manufacture, and delivery of short/medium range sub-orbital vehicle configurations, including provision of ground test hardware, special test equipment, materials and required engineering support and launch support services. Work will be performed in Mooresville, North Carolina (37%); White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico (24%); Glen Burnie, Maryland (20%); Benbecula, Scotland (6%), Las Cruces, New Mexico (4%); Woomera, Australia (3%); Conroe, Texas (2%); Huntsville, Alabama (1%); San Nicolas Island, California (1%); Kekaha, Hawaii (1%); and Wallops Island, Virginia (1%), and is expected to be completed by July 2027. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test, and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $9,250,500 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Surface Warfare Center, Port Hueneme, White Sands Detachment, Port Hueneme, California, is the contracting activity.

L3Harris Technologies Integrated Systems L.P., doing business as Aeromet, Tulsa, Oklahoma, is being awarded an indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract with a maximum amount of $499,573,000. Under this follow-on contract, the contractor will provide support for the Missile Defense Agency Flight Test Airborne Sensors (ABS) program. These efforts will continue operations and sustainment of the flight test ABS aircraft and sensor equipment, mission planning and flight test execution, and Improvement and Modernization efforts. The work will be performed in Tulsa, Oklahoma. One initial task order in the amount of $22,175,032 is being issued. The ordering period is from Sept. 15, 2026, through Sept. 14, 2036. This contract was competitively procured via publication on the Governmentwide Point of Entry website with one proposal received. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $5,000,000 are being obligated on this award. The Missile Defense Agency, Huntsville, Alabama, is the contracting activity (HQ0855-26-D-E001).

Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems, Moorestown, New Jersey, was awarded a $60,602,848 cost-plus-award-fee, cost-plus-fixed-fee, and cost (no-fee) contract for AEGIS ship integration and test in support of surface combatant ships and related tactical sites. This contract includes options which, if exercised, would bring the cumulative value of this contract to $1,383,266,817. Work will be performed in Moorestown, New Jersey (36%); Norfolk, Virginia Beach (25%); Bath, Maine (11%); Pascagoula, Mississippi (10%); San Diego, California (9%); Deveselu, Romania (4%); Redzikowo, Poland (3%); and various other locations (2%), and is expected to be completed by June 2027. If all options are exercised, work will continue through June 2036. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $8,241,953 (43%); fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $5,099,931 (27%); fiscal 2024 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $3,117,108 (16%); fiscal 2020 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $797,786 (4%); fiscal 2017 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $716,800 (4%); fiscal 2023 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount $692,633 (4%); and fiscal 2021 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $370,891 (2%), will be obligated at time of award, of which $8,241,953 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the System for Award Management website, with two offers received. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N00024-26-C-5341). (Awarded June 30, 2026).

Thoma-Sea Marine Constructors LLC,* Houma, Louisiana, is awarded $26,625,622 firm-fixed-price modification to a previously awarded contract (N00024-19-C-2216) for the definitization of an engineering change related to the shore power configuration and capability for both National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Auxiliary general Oceanographic Research Variant Ship One and Two and the settlement of other ship changes. Work will be performed in Houma, Louisiana, and is expected to be completed by November 2028. Procurement, acquisition, and construction (NOAA) funds in the amount of $26,625,622 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N00024-19-C-2216).

Information Systems and Networks Corp., Bethesda, Maryland, is awarded a $20,983,333 firm-fixed-price and cost task order (M9549426F0006) against the General Services Administration One Acquisition Solution for Integrated Services Plus (OASIS+) indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract (47QRCA25DU164) to provide housing property management support services for Marine Corps service members residing in unaccompanied housing. Work will be performed at 26 installations located in both the continental U.S.; and outside the continental U.S., including Okinawa, Japan (23%); Oceanside, California (21%); Jacksonville, North Carolina (21%); San Diego, California (6%); Port Royal, South Carolina (5%); 29 Palms, California (4%); Kaneohe, Hawaii (4%); Quantico, Virginia (4%); Havelock, North Carolina (3%); Yuma, Arizona (3%); and with various other locations making up less than 1%. This task order includes options which, if exercised, would bring the cumulative value of this task order to $144,141,182. If all options are exercised, work will continue through January 2031. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance (Marine Corps) funds in the amount of $20,983,333 will be obligated at time of award and will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This task order was awarded on a competitive basis in accordance with the terms of the GSA OASIS+ multiple award contract program and three proposals were received. The Marine Corps Installations Command Contracting Office, Arlington, Virginia, is the contracting activity (M9549425D0001).

Global Air Logistics and Training Aerospace Inc.,* San Diego, California, is awarded a $13,228,748 modification (P00003) to a firm-fixed-price, cost-plus-fixed-fee, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract (N0001925D1117). This modification increases the contract ceiling for production and delivery of up to 20 SkyTower II production Airborne Network Extension Air Vehicle kits (A-Kits) and associated installation efforts in support of the Marine Corps airborne networking capabilities. Work will be performed in San Diego, California (54%); Cherry Point, North Carolina (3%); Yuma, Arizona (3%); and various locations outside the continental U.S. (40%), and is expected to be completed in September 2030. No funds will be obligated at the time of award; funds will be obligated on individual orders as they are issued. This contract was not competed. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

Applied Physical Electronics LC,* Spicewood, Texas, is awarded a $9,620,094 modification (P00003) to a previously awarded cost-plus-fixed-fee contract (N0042126C0012). This modification exercises an option to provide for the development, fabrication, installation, and acceptance testing of upgrades to the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division's Vertical Electromagnetic Pulse Simulator in support of improved reliability, ensuring compliance with current testing standards, enhancing testing capability, and expanding the simulator's capacity to accommodate larger and taller test assets for the Navy. Work will be performed in Spicewood, Texas (85%); and Patuxent River, Maryland (15%), and is expected to be completed in January 2029. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Defense Wide) funds in the amount of $2,912,000 will be obligated at time of award. This contract was not completed. Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

Lockheed Martin Aeronautics Co., Marietta, Georgia, has been awarded a $142,910,785 cost-plus-fixed-fee and firm-fixed price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for software sustainment services for the C-5 Galaxy. This contract provides software updates and maintenance, supporting certification artifacts, systems integration laboratory maintenance, engineering and technical support, and software engineering support services. Work will be performed in Marietta, Georgia; and Greenville, South Carolina, and is expected to be completed by May 20, 2032. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2026 operation and maintenance funds in the amount of $19,317,604 are being obligated at time of award. The C-5 Contracting Branch, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, is the contracting activity (FA8525-26-D-B002).
